correctness.rationale: The source equations reduce exactly to a two-dimensional linear map with trace \([2+2t-\kappa^2t^2]/(1+t)^2\) and determinant \(1/(1+t)^2\). The three Jury inequalities leave exactly \(4+4t+(1-\kappa^2)t^2>0\), giving all-step stability for \(0<\kappa\le1\) and the sharp ceiling \(2/(\kappa-1)\) for \(\kappa>1\). The discriminant changes sign only once at the stated \(t_\star\). Before it the root modulus is \(1/(1+t)\); after it, an exact scaled-root derivative inequality proves strict increase. The boundary root and full-resolvent contrast were independently replayed by the packaged checker.

value.rationale: The source motivates implicit updates by enhanced stability, so determining whether block-sequential implicitness retains the canonical all-step stability of full proximal point is a natural structural question. The result finds an exact coupling threshold \(c=a\): below it every positive step is stable, above it a finite \(-1\) flip boundary appears. It also identifies the unique rate-optimal step and shows that taking the step larger than the root-collision point slows the method even before instability. This separates two forms of implicitness in a minimal strongly convex--strongly concave model and supplies concrete parameter-design information.
